blocks.caption: Boolean searches, types of online research and digital literacy (original diagram after topic 8.1).
blocks.long_description: AND returns only pages containing both words, the overlap of the two circles, so it narrows a search; OR returns pages with either word, the whole of both circles, so it widens a search; NOT returns pages with the first word but not the second, cutting the overlap away. Online research may be general, academic, market, fact-checking or health research. Digital literacy combines using technology, searching, evaluating sources, creating content and staying safe and private.

blocks.prompt: Discuss the types of online research and their purposes, with examples (long question 1).
blocks.explanation: General information research gives an overview, for example searching Google to understand what renewable energy is. Academic research finds expert, detailed sources for study, such as journal articles on pollution for a project. Market research helps businesses understand trends, customers and competition, such as a shop checking demand for a new product. Fact-checking confirms whether a claim is true by comparing reliable sources, such as checking a viral news story. Health research finds information on symptoms and treatments from trusted medical sites and journals.

items: Five types: general, academic, market, fact-checking, health.
